chapter: Fellow musicians and brass band world
title: George's three jobs and little sleep
summary: Talk of how a drummer named George juggled theatre, wax museum and music jobs, despite his boss's urging.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: You don't like the maple there? No. I used to carry two glasses at once in case I ran out. They really wore it on. They had a good time. Yeah, it was nice. They always liked Joyce. Yeah, they did. Everybody liked Joyce. I don't see how you worked. I mean, that man. How many jobs would he play? And work?
He was working at the theater. When he'd get off from the theater, he would go to the wax museum, work there. Then go play music all night. And then play a parade?
And play a parade, that's right. Yeah. Can you imagine? That's right.
Three and four jobs. That's right. That's right. And he still find time to get in trouble, I mean. Find time to go around all them women's he had. Oh, that man was so good.

He used to tell me about all the different places he'd be at home. You know, I mean, just for kicks, he'd be going around all these places. That's right. And yet I knew he'd be working three jobs. I couldn't see how he could work in the paddock, and clean up the theaters, and clean up the wax museum, and still have time for all that fun.

That's right. He sure did. He sure did. When did he sleep? Sure again, the- He got about an hour or so sleep with him. That's what his boss told me. I played for them at Prince Coni. I went out and he said, he used to tell George all the time, he's doing too much work. He said, George, your in-laws, haunt. Who told you that? Mr. Lazarus. Oh, yeah. And he said that he told George to quit doing all that work. If he needed that money, call him to him. He would help his mom, he said, doing all that work. Say, all right, come and clean up the show in the morning. Then go home and go to rest. Then go to work at night. All that wax museum and all that. What George said, George, he had his heart. He wouldn't do it.
He'd have his little grandson, a great-grandson or something. Yeah, little grandson, yeah. His grandson, I remember that.
